title: Night Lights: 2012–2023
subtitle: Global Urban Illumination Dynamics
credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Visualizer: Kel Elkins. Scientists: Zhuosen Wang, Miguel Román, Ranjay Shrestha, Srija Chakraborty, Virginia Kalb.

mappingCard.whatYouSee: Global flat map view of night lights from 2012 to 2023 transitioning into decadal change: purple areas indicate brightening cities and expanding electrification, while orange areas show dimmed lighting.
mappingCard.howItSounds: A minor pentatonic plucked notes with stereo panning across longitude. Playback tempo accelerates dynamically as active lit area density increases.
mappingCard.scaleAndTempo: A minor pentatonic (A, C, D, E, G), 70-130 BPM dynamic tempo.
mappingCard.limits: Sonifies rendered RGB pixel luminance from visualization stills, not raw calibrated sensor radiance (nanowatt/cm²·sr).

title: ISS Lightning: 2017–2023
subtitle: Global Tropical & Mid-Latitude Flash Events
credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Visualizers: Michala Garrison, Greg Shirah, Kel Elkins, Alex Kekesi.

mappingCard.source: NASA EIC / SVS #5011 (ISS Lightning Imaging Sensor)
mappingCard.whatYouSee: Global lightning strikes detected from the International Space Station over a 6-year period with a 10-day roving window highlighting seasonal storm migrations across equatorial belts.
mappingCard.howItSounds: Percussive noise bursts and bright sine pings triggered by detected flash clusters; pitch mapped to latitude (blob Y) and pan mapped to longitude (blob X).
mappingCard.scaleAndTempo: D Dorian mode (D, E, F, G, A, B, C), event-driven percussive timing.
mappingCard.limits: Sonifies optical flash clusters from 10-day composite frames, not instant millisecond electrical discharges.

title: Ocean Currents: Western Boundary
subtitle: Perpetual Ocean High-Resolution Flow
credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Visualizers: Greg Shirah, Horace Mitchell. Technical Support: Laurence Schuler, Ian Jones. Scientists: Atousa Saberi, Josh Willis. Producer: Kathleen Gaeta.

mappingCard.source: NASA EIC / SVS #5425 (ECCO2 Ocean Model Synthesis)
mappingCard.whatYouSee: 3D velocity field particle trails visualizing powerful western boundary currents (Kuroshio, Agulhas retroflection, Gulf Stream) and oceanic eddies.
mappingCard.howItSounds: Four detuned triangle voices generating an evolving oceanic ambient chord; root frequency drifts with mean water hue, while flow velocity modulates LFO and filter sweeps.
mappingCard.scaleAndTempo: D Dorian (D3, F3, A3, C4) ambient pad, 75 BPM flow modulation.
mappingCard.limits: Sonifies rendered particle tracer velocity colors, not physical hydrographic temperature and salinity measurements.

title: Global CO2 Plume: 2020
subtitle: DYAMOND Atmospheric Circulation & Emissions
credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Visualizers: AJ Christensen, Greg Shirah, Helen-Nicole Kostis, Mark SubbaRao. Technical Support: Laurence Schuler, Ian Jones. Scientists: Lesley Ott, Brad Weir, William Putman, Tomohiro Oda.

mappingCard.source: NASA EIC / SVS #5196 (GEOS Model / DYAMOND Simulation)
mappingCard.whatYouSee: Global atmospheric carbon dioxide plumes swirling through weather patterns from January through March 2020, rising from industrial centers and fires.
mappingCard.howItSounds: Dynamic harmonic chord tension: low concentrations produce a warm Major 7th chord; mid concentrations introduce a 9th; high concentrations inject minor 2nd and tritone dissonance.
mappingCard.scaleAndTempo: Dynamic harmonic tension scale (Major 7th to Tritone dissonance), 84 BPM.
mappingCard.limits: Sonifies rendered 3D point cloud opacity and color ramp, not direct atmospheric flask parts-per-million measurements.
